title: Man. Post. Cap. IV: GAR Resp. — eternal torment vs proper death
pass_a_gloss: GAR. Reply. The learned man acknowledges that by the name of death both corporal death and also the eternal torment of hell are understood, as we have heard. What then will he answer, if someone throws back this argument at him: that the same voice in a law which ought to be conceived in usual words cannot be taken at once properly and metaphorically: but that the torment of hell is death spoken metaphorically, since only corporal death is death properly so called: therefore that torment cannot be understood by these words.
pass_b_english: GAR. Reply. The learned man grants that 'death' covers both bodily death and the eternal torment of hell, as we have heard. What then will he say if someone turns his own argument back on him: the same word in a law that should use ordinary language cannot be taken properly and metaphorically together; hell's torment is death only metaphorically, since only bodily death is death properly so called; therefore those words cannot mean that torment.
source_text: GAR. Resp. Agnoscit Vir doctus, mortis nomine, tum mortem corporalem, tum etiam aeternum inferorum cruciatum intelligi, ut audivimus. Quid ergo responsurus est, si quis hoc argumentum ipsi reponat; vocem eandem in lege, quae debeat verbis usitatis concipi, non posse simul proprie & metaphorice sumi: cruciatum autem inferorum esse mortem metaphorice dictam, cum sola corporalis sit mors proprie dicta: ergo non posse his verbis intelligi cruciatum illum.

choices.choice: turns dual-sense objection against eternal torment
